title: Family Road Trip Vietnam: Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh
excerpt: A north-to-south Vietnam road trip is one of Asia's great family adventures. From Hanoi's ancient streets to the limestone karsts of Ha Long Bay, the lantern-lit town of Hoi An, and the energy of Ho Chi Minh City, here's a 14-day itinerary designed for families with kids.
author: Family Travel Asia Team
content:
A north-to-south road trip through Vietnam is one of Asia's great family adventures. It covers over 1,600 kilometers through stunning landscapes — from the misty mountains of Sapa to the limestone karsts of Ha Long Bay, the ancient town of Hoi An, and the dynamic energy of Ho Chi Minh City. The best part? Vietnam is incredibly affordable, the food is kid-friendly, and the locals absolutely adore children.

This 14-day itinerary is designed for families with kids aged 3–14, balancing driving time with play breaks, cultural stops with kid-friendly activities, and including real prices so you can budget accurately.

**Note on transport:** While trains and flights cover the Hanoi–Ho Chi Minh route faster, a road trip (using private drivers or domestic flights + rental cars between segments) gives you flexibility and lets you stop at small towns and roadside attractions.

**Cost summary for a family of 4:** Accommodation $400–700, food $200–350, transport $300–500, activities $150–300 = **total ~$1,050–1,850 for 14 days**. That's $75–132 per day for the whole family!

## Days 1–3: Hanoi

**📍 Northern Vietnam**

Start your journey in Hanoi, Vietnam's charming capital. The Old Quarter's narrow streets are chaotic but magical — each street named after the goods historically sold there (Silk Street, Paper Street, etc.).

**Family-friendly activities:**
- **Hoan Kiem Lake** — A peaceful walk around the lake (free). Your kids will love seeing the giant tortoises at the temple on the island.
- **Vietnam Museum of Ethnology** (entrance: VND 40,000 / US$1.60) — Excellent indoor activity with interactive exhibits on Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups.
- **Water Puppet Theatre** (Thang Long Theatre, tickets: VND 100,000 / US$4.00) — A uniquely Vietnamese art form that mesmerizes kids. Shows run 45 minutes.
- **Train Street** — Watch the train squeeze through a narrow residential alley. Free to watch; buy a drink at a café for ~US$1.

**Where to eat with kids:**
- **Bun Cha Huong Lien** (Obama's famous bun cha stop) — VND 50,000 / US$2.00 per bowl. Kids love the grilled pork and rice noodles.
- **Pho Gia Truyen** (49 Bat Dan) — Legendary pho, VND 60,000 / US$2.40.
- **Note:** Vietnamese street food is generally safe, but stick to busy stalls with high turnover. Most pho and noodle dishes are mild — skip the chili if your kids aren't ready.

**Accommodation:** Try **Hanoi Elegance Ruby Hotel** in the Old Quarter (~$35–55/night for family room) for its central location and helpful staff.

## Day 3–4: Ha Long Bay / Lan Ha Bay

**📍 2.5-hour drive east of Hanoi**

No trip to Vietnam is complete without seeing Ha Long Bay's iconic limestone islands. For families, we recommend **Lan Ha Bay** (a quieter alternative to Ha Long Bay) or a **one-night cruise**.

**Family cruise options:** Many operators offer 2-day/1-night cruises. We recommend **Paradise Cruises** or **Bhaya Cruises** for their family cabins and kid-friendly activities.

**Cost:** ~$150–250 per adult, kids aged 4–11 at 50–75% of adult price, under 4s free. Includes all meals, kayaking, cave visits, and squid fishing.

**Stroller tip:** You won't need a stroller on the boat — the space is tight. Bring a baby carrier for cave visits. The boat deck is safe for toddlers with supervision.

## Days 5–8: Hoi An

**📍 Central Vietnam (fly Hanoi–Da Nang, ~US$30–50/person, then 30-min taxi to Hoi An)**

Hoi An is the highlight for many families. This UNESCO-listed ancient town is charming, pedestrian-friendly, and has a beautiful river running through it.

**Family-friendly activities:**
- **Old Town walking** — Entry requires a ticket (VND 120,000 / US$4.80 for adults, kids under 6 free) which covers 5 of 21 attractions including Japanese Covered Bridge and old merchant houses.
- **Lantern-making class** (from VND 150,000 / US$6.00 per person) — Taxi drivers wear colorful lanterns. Most workshops are 1–2 hours. **Thu Bon Lantern** is highly recommended for families.
- **An Bang Beach** — 4km east of Old Town, free entry, sunbeds ~US$3–5. Great for a beach day.
- **Cooking class** (from VND 500,000 / US$20 per adult, kids 50% off) — **Hoi An Eco Cooking Class** includes a market tour, river boat ride, and hands-on cooking.
- **Tra Que Vegetable Village** — Free to walk around, see farmers working with traditional methods. Kids can try planting vegetables for VND 50,000 / US$2.

**Where to eat with kids:**
- **Banh Mi Phuong** (Anthony Bourdain–endorsed) — The best banh mi in town, VND 30,000 / US$1.20. Kids love the simple grilled pork version.
- **Morning Glory Restaurant** — Family-friendly Vietnamese classics. Cao lau noodles (~VND 80,000 / US$3.20) are mild and kid-friendly.
- **Cargo Club Cafe** — Great for Western breakfast options if your kids need a familiar break.

**Stroller tip:** The Old Town streets are mostly pedestrianized from 3–9 PM, making strolling easy. Some bridges have steps. A lightweight umbrella stroller works best.

**Accommodation:** **Hoi An Riverside Resort & Spa** (~$45–70/night) has a great pool, kids' club, and river views.

## Days 9–10: Da Nang (Stop on the way south)

**📍 1-hour drive from Hoi An**

Da Nang has some of Vietnam's best family attractions:
- **Ba Na Hills** (cable car up the mountain, entrance ~$30/adult, $15/child) — Features the famous Golden Bridge (giant stone hands), a French village, and an indoor amusement park for kids. The cable car ride is an experience in itself.
- **My Khe Beach** — Free, beautiful white sand, gentle waves suitable for children.
- **Son Tra Peninsula (Monkey Mountain)** — Free to drive through, wild monkeys everywhere. Keep windows up and don't feed them.

## Days 11–14: Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) & Mekong Delta

**📍 Southern Vietnam (fly Da Nang–HCMC, ~US$25–45/person)**

Ho Chi Minh City is the energetic finale to your road trip. It's busier than Hanoi, but the attractions are well worth it.

**Family-friendly activities:**
- **HCMC Museum** (VND 40,000 / US$1.60) — Important for older kids (10+). The outdoor aircraft display is fascinating. Skip the more graphic exhibits for younger children.
- **historical sites** (half-day tour, ~$15–25/person including transport) — Kids can crawl through the narrow tunnels, see booby traps, and try shooting an AK-47 ($1.60 per 10 bullets at the range). Best for ages 7+.
- **Saigon Zoo & Botanical Gardens** (VND 60,000 / US$2.40, under 1m tall free) — One of the world's oldest zoos, dated but charming. The botanical gardens are lovely for a quiet stroll.
- **Binh Tay Market** (Chinatown) — A sensory explosion. Free to wander, great for souvenirs. Kids love the dried fruit snacks.
- **Ben Thanh Street Food Market** — Night market with live music, great pho and spring rolls. Most dishes US$2–4.

**Mekong Delta Day Trip (~$20–30/person)** — Take a boat through the canals, visit coconut candy workshops, and sample tropical fruits. Most tour operators pick up from HCMC hotels. The sampan ride through narrow canals is a highlight for kids.

## Vietnam Road Trip Tips for Families

### Getting Around
- **Long distances:** Book private drivers through your hotel (~$40–60/day for a car with AC). Most drivers speak basic English and will stop whenever you ask.
- **Trains:** The Reunification Express connects Hanoi and HCMC, but it's slow (30+ hours). Choose the overnight sleeper for a fun experience — soft sleeper bunks are ~$30–50/person.
- **Domestic flights:** Vietnam Airlines, VietJet, and Bamboo Airways are all reliable. Book 2–4 weeks ahead for best prices.

### Food & Water
- Stick to bottled water (VND 5,000–10,000 / US$0.20–0.40 from any shop).
- Pho, banh mi, rice dishes, and spring rolls are universally kid-approved.
- Many restaurants serve "western menu" items (pizza, pasta, fries) if needed.

### Health
- Recommended vaccinations: Hepatitis A, Typhoid, Tetanus.
- Mosquito repellent is essential, especially in the Mekong Delta.
- Pharmacies are everywhere and well-stocked.

### Best Time to Go
- **October–April:** Dry season across Vietnam. Cooler in the north, warm in the south.
- **May–September:** Hot and rainy. Still travelable but expect afternoon downpours.

Vietnam is an incredible family road trip destination — affordable, safe, and endlessly fascinating for kids of all ages. The memories of navigating Hanoi's Old Quarter in a cyclo, watching your kids' faces as a giant whale shark passes by at the aquarium, and eating banh mi on a Hoi An street corner will stay with your family forever.
